cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Reveal the Truth in Layers
cards.instruction: Protect someone by disclosing the truth in stages, changing what each earlier statement appears to mean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've turned the venue letter face down like the planner. Our wedding still has a date.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She turned a menu over to show us the prices. Why can't I see the letter?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, one page at a time. The date's ours; we'll need a different building.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did they give our booking away?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. There was a fire. We haven't lost the day, just the place; let me sit with you while you read it.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies face-down document handling as professional news control; A3 saves face through one-page-at-time while turning reassurance into venue loss; A5 gives the fire truth with direct support for B.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 access challenge causes A3 partial disclosure; B4 booking-loss theory prompts A5 cause and reassurance about the retained date.

relationship.evidence: B4 tries to understand an apparent lost booking, a plausible practical concern.

heightening.evidence: A5 changes A3 unavailable building into fire damage while offering to share the difficult reading.

specificity.evidence: A1 wedding letter and B2 planner/menu distinguish copied gestures; B4 booking identifies what B fears.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 no/fire/day/place/sit is longer but each part corrects B4 and offers support rather than merely explaining disclosure technique.
